The Bende Socio-Political Forum said the criminal case against Okorie was being handled by the police and should not be presented as a personal prosecution by the Deputy Speaker.
The group stated this in a statement signed by its President, Hon. David Munachi, and Secretary, Comrade Nnamdi Ikechukwu, on Tuesday.
It said the charge sheet before the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Charge No. FHC/ABJ/CR/710/2026, listed the Inspector-General of Police as the complainant and Okorie as the defendant.
According to the forum, Kalu was only a nominal complainant in the matter, urging members of the public to examine the court documents before drawing conclusions about the case.
The organisation also addressed concerns surrounding Okorie’s reported physical disability, saying his condition should not prevent the investigation of allegations against him.
It, however, stressed that his dignity, medical needs and constitutional rights must be respected throughout the judicial process.
“Being physically challenged does not place anybody above the law or automatically exempt a person from answering allegations of criminal conduct,” the statement read.
The forum also maintained that Okorie remained innocent until proven guilty by a competent court.
On the allegations surrounding ₦348 million reportedly meant for a garri-processing plant in Umuhu Ezechi, the group said claims of financial wrongdoing should be supported with verifiable evidence, including financial records and audit reports.
It further said some publications allegedly made by Okorie on the Umuhu Ezechi Development Union WhatsApp platform formed part of the issues surrounding the case.
The forum maintained that Kalu, despite his position as Deputy Speaker, retained the right to protect his reputation against allegations it considered defamatory.
It also expressed concern that the controversy could be exploited for political purposes ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The organisation called on the police and judiciary to handle the matter professionally and without political interference, while urging the media to distinguish between allegations and established facts.
It said the court remained the appropriate place to determine the merits of the case.
